# Country and cross-country research playbook

## Purpose

Establish the conditions that matter for business opportunities in the country or countries the user named. Do not write a generic country report; connect conditions to jobs-to-be-done, buyers, market structure and execution feasibility.

## Country snapshot structure

For each country, assess relevant items from the following categories:

1. **Economy and household conditions:** disposable income proxies, inflation, wages, interest rates, credit availability, household spending mix and affordability.
2. **Demographics and household change:** age structure, migration, urbanisation, household size, aging, education and workforce participation where relevant.
3. **Business environment:** SME composition, business registrations, industry structure, labor shortages, productivity constraints, formal/informal market dynamics.
4. **Digital and physical infrastructure:** internet/smartphone/payment adoption, cloud/software adoption, logistics, electricity reliability, broadband, shipping and service coverage.
5. **Regulation and policy:** taxes, compliance, licensing, safety standards, import rules, data/privacy requirements, subsidies, incentives and procurement changes.
6. **Trade and value chains:** imported goods/components, local manufacturing, supply concentration, price movements, trade barriers, trade deficits/surpluses by relevant product code.
7. **Climate, environment and resources:** water, energy, waste, disaster adaptation, crop/food loss and other material needs.
8. **Public service and infrastructure gaps:** healthcare, education, transport, housing, local government, permitting and citizen-service pain.
9. **Technology and industry shifts:** new capabilities, declining costs, adoption changes, standards, vendor platform changes and workflow digitisation.
10. **Distribution and trust:** channels through which customers already buy, local-language needs, payments, marketplaces, incumbents, community networks and procurement norms.

Not all categories need to be researched for every country. Choose based on the signals.

## Country-specific source discovery

Start from official statistical systems, regulators and economic institutions. Example starting points (verify coverage and definitions before use):

- Global development indicators: https://data.worldbank.org/ and https://api.worldbank.org/v2/
- World Bank DataBank: https://databank.worldbank.org/
- IMF data: https://www.imf.org/en/Data
- OECD data: https://data.oecd.org/ and https://data-explorer.oecd.org/
- UN Comtrade: https://comtradeplus.un.org/ and https://comtradeapi.un.org/
- ILO statistics: https://ilostat.ilo.org/data/
- WTO statistics: https://stats.wto.org/
- UN Data: https://data.un.org/
- Eurostat: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/data/database
- US Census data: https://www.census.gov/data.html
- US Bureau of Labor Statistics: https://www.bls.gov/data/
- US Small Business Administration: https://www.sba.gov/business-guide
- UK Office for National Statistics: https://www.ons.gov.uk/
- UK Companies House: https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/
- India Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation: https://www.mospi.gov.in/
- India Reserve Bank of India: https://www.rbi.org.in/
- India data.gov.in: https://www.data.gov.in/
- India Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence and Statistics: https://www.dgciskol.gov.in/
- UAE Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Centre: https://fcsc.gov.ae/
- UAE Central Bank: https://www.centralbank.ae/
- Singapore Department of Statistics: https://www.singstat.gov.sg/
- Australia Bureau of Statistics: https://www.abs.gov.au/
- Statistics Canada: https://www.statcan.gc.ca/

This is a starter catalogue, not a claim that every endpoint is live, downloadable or suitable for every request. Check access date, methodology, definitions, licensing and update cadence.

## Cross-country fairness

- Use comparable metrics, definitions, currency periods and populations where possible.
- Convert currencies only when a common currency is useful; record exchange-rate source and date.
- Normalize per capita, per firm or per household only when denominator data is reliable.
- Do not rank a country higher because it has more English-language complaints or more accessible data.
- Make separate judgments for market attractiveness, source coverage and execution difficulty.
- For a country comparison, note localisation, taxes, language, payment systems, sales channels, regulation, fulfillment and support requirements.

## Local language research

Use local-language terms for a material problem and competitor category when it may change coverage. Translate quotes or search findings conservatively and label translations. Do not fabricate translated first-person quotes. Preserve the original link and, if useful, short original phrase.

## Market-change interpretation

For a change in law or policy, distinguish announcement, approval, publication and enforcement/effective dates. For a market or consumer trend, seek a baseline and compare like-for-like periods. For product launches, verify whether availability is general, limited beta, region-restricted or merely announced.

## From condition to business hypothesis

A macro trend is not an opportunity by itself. Connect it through a chain:

`documented change -> affected actor -> newly painful/expensive task -> current workaround/spend -> buyer and budget -> plausible offer -> reachable channel`

If one of the links is unknown, mark it explicitly and design the next research question around it.
